swaps.old_row: | J-A28.34 | Chose to build a transient arena's input rings as exact topology — a lattice point two rings share one vertex, a side two rings share one edge, a vertex within the hot pixel of another ring's side splitting that side, no attraction — refusing with `E_DEGENERATE` (detail `seed`, `fixed` or `overlap`) a ring that would break `minEdge`, clearance or simplicity and any overlap, which one winding walk finds; to require seed rings that tile, a caller whose wings overlap passing each clipped against the wings before it; and to require each fixed ring inside one seed ring — over inserting the rings as `mandatory` chains under §3.6's attraction, as J-A28.31 first chose, and over accepting overlapping seeds, or fixed rings anywhere in the seeds' union. Attraction would move a kept room on a re-cut: an earlier cut may split a vertex onto a wall 25.29–26 cm from its corner (§3.2 (2)), and re-inserting it would move it onto that corner, so J-A28.33's promise that a kept room re-enters unchanged would fail for a share of rooms; a refusal is typed and caught by F-PLAN (§5.2) where a silent move would change a kept room. Overlapping seeds would count their overlap twice in the tiling check, enclose it in fixed edges no merge may delete (a forced room) and make `readBack`'s seed tags ambiguous; a fixed ring across the joint between two wings would be split by it into two faces, although a fixed ring is a face no cut divides. The construction is a second door for edges beside `insertChain`, confined to a transient arena's opening as §3.9's load is to a stored plat. Every vertex a face partitioner places on a fixed edge is placed against the input sides that edge lies on, as passed — the input sides are the arena's routes, as a plat's coarser route is for the Steiner vertices on it — over placing it against the sub-edge an earlier split left, because on a one-level arena each sub-edge would be its own route, and same-level splits of a rotated side then drift its later vertices beyond the hot pixel of the straight line, where the construction cannot split the side when a kept room re-enters and refuses the room (a model of §3.6's rule: one side in nine split four times, worst 1.6 cm, `docs/validation/bench/amendb_verify_kernel_r1_drift.out`; placed against the input side, no vertex beyond the hot pixel, no failed search and no refused kept corner over 400 000 splits, `docs/validation/bench/amendb_repair_kernel_r2_routes.out`). Overlapping wings are clipped as the faces of one overlay of the storey's rings, each face going to the first ring in wing order that contains it (`tileRings`), over one `booleans('difference', …)` per ring, because separate overlays leave an earlier ring without the crossing vertices a later one gains and can place a T's second crossing off the bar's straight side (1.3 % of cases, worst 1.06 cm), refusing a valid building's seeds; one overlay gives every ring each crossing vertex, so the joints are shared vertex for vertex. A piece left with a hole — an earlier wing wholly inside a later one — is refused, because a seed is one ring and which wing takes the enclosed rooms is the plan rung's choice, not the kernel's. It amends J-A28.31's insertion and J-A28.33's claim that a kept room reads back byte-identical: a new wall ending on a kept room adds a vertex within the hot pixel of its side, so the room keeps its polygon — its vertices unmoved and in order — rather than its bytes (§3.4, §3.10; items 28, 28 (f); repair-kernel-r1 after verify-kernel-r0's VK-02 and VK-03; amended by repair-kernel-r2 after verify-kernel-r1's VK1-01 and VK1-10). |
